\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सासू} (sāsū)}{सासू (sāsū)}]{\mw{सासू} (sāsū) — a mother-in-law}

\label{lesson:MW-C259-sasu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to bear (pain), then the Marwadi for the heart (as the seat of feeling).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सासू}}
\textbf{\mw{सासू}} — \emph{sāsū} — \textquotedblleft{}a mother-in-law\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हारी} \mw{सासू} \mw{घणी} \mw{भली} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhārī sāsū ghaṇī bhalī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother-in-law is very kind.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{सासू}} (\emph{sāsū}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{śvaśrū}, \textquotedblleft{}a husband's or wife's mother\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{sāsū} (CDIAL 12759).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāsū}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāsū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhārī sāsū ghaṇī bhalī hai.} — My mother-in-law is very kind.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to bear (pain), then the Marwadi for the heart (as the seat of feeling), then say \emph{sāsū} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{सासू} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mother-in-law\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{धणी} (dhaṇī)}{धणी (dhaṇī)}]{\mw{धणी} (dhaṇī) — a husband (in his wife's words); a master}

\label{lesson:MW-C259-dhani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a husband's younger brother, then the Marwadi for a husband's sister.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{धणी}}
\textbf{\mw{धणी}} — \emph{dhaṇī} — \textquotedblleft{}a husband (in his wife's words); a master\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हारो} \mw{धणी} \mw{खेत} \mw{गयो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My husband went to the field.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{धणी}} (\emph{dhaṇī}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{dhanin}, \textquotedblleft{}rich\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{dhaṇī̃}, \textquotedblleft{}owner\textquotedblright{}, Old Marwari \emph{dhaṇī}, \textquotedblleft{}master\textquotedblright{}, and Gujarati \emph{dhaṇī}, \textquotedblleft{}husband\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 6722).

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from At the Healer's to My Husband's Family}

\label{lesson:MW-R259-review-254-259}



\begin{quote}
Say the Marwadi for a traditional healer and a pill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a traditional healer, a pill, to swell up, rest, sluggishness
  \item one's health, to get worse, to get better, a tear (from the eye), to tremble
  \item to be afraid, sorrow, contentment, joy, high spirits
  \item anger, to sulk, modesty, a sigh, a reproach
  \item worry, trust, patience, to bear (pain), the heart (as the seat of feeling)
  \item a mother-in-law, a father-in-law, a husband's younger brother, a husband's sister, a husband (in his wife's words)
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A traditional healer? (\textbf{\mw{वैद}}, \emph{vaid}.) A pill? (\textbf{\mw{गोळी}}, \emph{goḷī}.) To swell up? (\textbf{\mw{सूजणो}}, \emph{sūjṇo}.) Rest? (\textbf{\mw{आराम}}, \emph{ārām}.) Sluggishness? (\textbf{\mw{आळस}}, \emph{āḷas}.) One's health? (\textbf{\mw{तबियत}}, \emph{tabiyat}.) To get worse? (\textbf{\mw{बिगड़णो}}, \emph{bigaṛṇo}.) To get better? (\textbf{\mw{सुधरणो}}, \emph{sudharṇo}.) A tear (from the eye)? (\textbf{\mw{आंसू}}, \emph{ā̃sū}.) To tremble? (\textbf{\mw{कांपणो}}, \emph{kā̃pṇo}.) To be afraid? (\textbf{\mw{डरणो}}, \emph{ḍarṇo}.) Sorrow? (\textbf{\mw{दुख}}, \emph{dukh}.) Contentment? (\textbf{\mw{सुख}}, \emph{sukh}.) Joy? (\textbf{\mw{आणंद}}, \emph{āṇand}.) High spirits? (\textbf{\mw{उमंग}}, \emph{umaṅg}.) Anger? (\textbf{\mw{रीस}}, \emph{rīs}.) To sulk? (\textbf{\mw{रूसणो}}, \emph{rūsṇo}.) Modesty? (\textbf{\mw{लाज}}, \emph{lāj}.) A sigh? (\textbf{\mw{निसासो}}, \emph{nisāso}.) A reproach? (\textbf{\mw{ओळमो}}, \emph{oḷmo}.) Worry? (\textbf{\mw{चिंता}}, \emph{chintā}.) Trust? (\textbf{\mw{भरोसो}}, \emph{bharoso}.) Patience? (\textbf{\mw{धीरज}}, \emph{dhīraj}.) To bear (pain)? (\textbf{\mw{सहणो}}, \emph{sahṇo}.) The heart (as the seat of feeling)? (\textbf{\mw{हियो}}, \emph{hiyo}.) A mother-in-law? (\textbf{\mw{सासू}}, \emph{sāsū}.) A father-in-law? (\textbf{\mw{सुसरो}}, \emph{susro}.) A husband's younger brother? (\textbf{\mw{देवर}}, \emph{devar}.) A husband's sister? (\textbf{\mw{नणद}}, \emph{naṇad}.) A husband (in his wife's words)? (\textbf{\mw{धणी}}, \emph{dhaṇī}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
